metadata.archetype_justification: Read-only CGI binary that looks up prices from a static flat file. No database connections, no cache writes, no user-specific state, no write operations.
metadata.context: Legacy C++ CGI pricing engine reading product prices from a flat file, served via Apache httpd on Kubernetes

findings.title: No Structured API — HTML-Only CGI Response
findings.description: The application exposes an HTTP CGI endpoint at /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi accepting query parameters sku and qty. The response format is text/html — raw HTML markup, not a structured machine-readable format. No API documentation exists. An agent would need to parse HTML output to extract pricing data.
findings.gap: No structured (JSON/XML) API response format. HTML output requires scraping for programmatic integration. No API documentation.
findings.recommendation: Add a JSON response mode triggered by an Accept: application/json header or format=json query parameter. Document the endpoint contract in an OpenAPI specification.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: Zero authentication mechanism exists at any layer. Any network-reachable client can call /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi without presenting credentials. No OAuth2, no API keys, no mTLS, no JWT verification, no API Gateway authorizer.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication. No principal attribution for audit. Cannot distinguish which agent or caller made a request.
findings.recommendation: Deploy an API Gateway in front of the service that requires API key or OAuth2 client credentials before forwarding requests.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions Model
findings.description: No authorization model exists. Since there is no authentication, there is no mechanism to scope permissions. All callers have identical, unrestricted access to all pricing data.
findings.gap: No permission scoping mechanism — cannot differentiate agent access levels.
findings.recommendation: After implementing authentication (AUTH-Q1), define tiered access via API Gateway usage plans.

compensating_controls: Kubernetes NetworkPolicy to restrict which pods can reach this service
API Gateway usage plans for tiered access

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. No RBAC, ABAC, or method-level controls at any layer.
findings.gap: Cannot restrict actions per caller identity.
findings.recommendation: Implement method-level auth at API Gateway (reject non-GET methods). Plan for future write controls.

compensating_controls: Service is currently read-only — no destructive actions possible
API Gateway method-level authorization when write endpoints are added

findings.title: No Rate Limiting Configured
findings.description: No rate limiting is configured at any layer. No API Gateway throttling, no WAF rules, no Ingress rate annotations, no application-level rate limiting. A runaway agent loop could send unlimited requests.
findings.gap: No rate limiting at the API layer. Agent traffic storms could overwhelm the service.
findings.recommendation: Add an Ingress resource with rate-limiting annotations, or deploy an API Gateway with throttling configuration.

compensating_controls: Kubernetes resource limits (CPU: 500m, Memory: 128Mi) provide implicit backpressure
Kubernetes Ingress with rate-limiting annotations

findings.title: No Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, Smithy model, or any machine-readable API specification exists in the repository.
findings.gap: No machine-readable specification for agent tool generation.
findings.recommendation: Create an openapi.yaml documenting the pricing endpoint: query parameters, response schema, and error cases.

compensating_controls: Manually author tool definition from code inspection
Use API Gateway OpenAPI export if deployed

findings.title: No Structured Error Responses
findings.description: All responses are HTTP 200 with HTML. Unknown SKU returns $0.00 with no error indication. No structured error codes, no retryable/terminal categorization.
findings.gap: No error codes, no distinction between success and failure, no structured error body.
findings.recommendation: Implement HTTP status codes (404, 400) and structured JSON error responses with error_code, message, and retryable fields.

compensating_controls: API Gateway can intercept and structure error responses
Thin proxy layer for response transformation

findings.title: No Input Validation — Buffer Overflow Risk
findings.description: Zero input validation. parse_query uses strcpy without bounds checking — SKU parameter can overflow 64-byte buffer. qty parsed with atoi (no range validation). Buffer overflow vulnerabilities confirmed in README.
findings.gap: No input validation at any layer. Malformed input accepted without validation or structured rejection.
findings.recommendation: Deploy API Gateway with request validation (SKU: max 64 chars alphanumeric, qty: positive integer 1-10000). Long-term: rewrite with safe string handling.

compensating_controls: WAF with request parameter validation rules
API Gateway request validators for parameter constraints

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No schema versioning, no API versioning, no contract testing. The endpoint URL has no version prefix. No changelog, no breaking change detection.
findings.gap: No versioning strategy. Agent tool bindings would break silently on any change.
findings.recommendation: Version the API (e.g., /v1/pricing) and document the response contract. Add changelog.

compensating_controls: Service is simple (one endpoint, two parameters) — changes are infrequent
Pin agent tool definitions to current behavior

findings.title: No Distributed Tracing or Structured Logging
findings.description: No distributed tracing (no X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry). No structured logging — CGI binary produces no logs. Apache produces unstructured access logs. No correlation IDs.
findings.gap: Cannot trace agent-initiated requests through the system.
findings.recommendation: Deploy Envoy or OTEL collector sidecar for request traces and structured JSON logs.

compensating_controls: Apache access logs provide basic request-level visibility
Envoy sidecar for trace injection and structured logs

findings.title: No Alerting on Error Rates or Latency
findings.description: No alerting configuration. No CloudWatch alarms, no Prometheus rules. Kubernetes probes provide health but no alerting thresholds.
findings.gap: Service degradation affecting agents would go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Deploy Prometheus with alerting rules or CloudWatch Container Insights with alarms.

compensating_controls: Kubernetes liveness/readiness probes restart unhealthy pods
Manual monitoring via kubectl

findings.title: IaC Without Review Gates or Drift Detection
findings.description: Kubernetes manifests in k8s/ define the deployment infrastructure as code. However, no peer review enforcement, no drift detection, no automated plan review. Manifests manually applied via kubectl.
findings.gap: IaC exists but lacks peer review gates and drift reconciliation.
findings.recommendation: Adopt GitOps (ArgoCD or Flux) to enforce PR review and drift reconciliation.

compensating_controls: K8s manifests provide declarative state
kubectl diff can detect drift

findings.title: No CI/CD Pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Makefile defines install target as manual SCP. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or CodeBuild. No contract testing.
findings.gap: No automated build, test, or contract validation before deployment.
findings.recommendation: Create CI pipeline (GitHub Actions or CodeBuild) with Docker build, smoke test, and ECR push.

compensating_controls: Dockerfile enables reproducible builds
Health check endpoint for manual validation

findings.title: Manual Rollback Only
findings.description: Kubernetes Deployment supports manual rollback via kubectl rollout undo. No automated rollback triggers, no canary deployment, no traffic shifting.
findings.gap: No automated rollback on failure. Manual operator intervention required.
findings.recommendation: Add Flagger or equivalent for metrics-based automated rollback.

compensating_controls: Kubernetes Deployment history preserves previous ReplicaSets
kubectl rollout undo provides fast manual recovery

findings.title: No Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment configuration. Dockerfile enables local container builds but no staging environment definition, no seed data, no environment separation.
findings.gap: No production-equivalent staging environment for agent testing.
findings.recommendation: Create staging namespace with test pricing rules and Kustomize overlays for environment separation.

compensating_controls: Docker build/run locally as minimal testing
Deploy same manifests to separate namespace

items.summary: Resolve BLOCKERs (structured API, machine identity) and critical RISK-SAFETY findings (scoped permissions, rate limiting) to unblock any agent integration.
Address RISK-QUALITY findings to improve agent effectiveness: API documentation, error handling, observability, and engineering maturity.
Address INFO findings as capacity allows for long-term agent architecture optimization.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy API Gateway with JSON response transformation and authentication
recommended_actions.rationale: An API Gateway addresses 5 findings simultaneously: adds structured JSON responses (API-Q1), machine identity via API keys (AUTH-Q1), scoped permissions via usage plans (AUTH-Q2, AUTH-Q3), rate limiting (STATE-Q5), and rate limit headers (API-Q8). This is the single highest-leverage remediation.

recommended_actions.action: Create OpenAPI specification and implement contract testing
recommended_actions.rationale: A machine-readable API spec enables automated agent tool generation and contract testing in CI.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy observability stack (tracing sidecar and alerting)
recommended_actions.rationale: Tracing and alerting are required to diagnose agent-initiated request failures and detect degradation.
GitOps adds peer review enforcement, drift detection, and automated rollback — closing infrastructure governance gaps.
